Source contracts: src/agent_runtime/runtime_guard_policy.py

src/agent_runtime/runtime_guard_policy.py

Python · Tier A

Resolve named Agent Checks while leaving enforcement with each subsystem owner.

Responsibilities

  • Define check metadata, supported scopes, effective values and versioned run overrides.

Boundaries

  • A guard policy changes a named controller check, not OS credentials, Gateway implementation availability or the truth of stored receipts.

Lifecycle

  • Settings/request admission produce an accepted snapshot; resolution overlays run overrides before the enforcement owner tests enabled state.

State

  • Frozen guard definitions are module metadata. Run snapshots, sources and revisions are persisted by their owning run/settings services.

Security

  • Validate guard identifiers against the registry and require strict booleans. Disabling credential enforcement still preserves diagnostic redaction obligations.

Collaborators

  • core/errors_msg.py supplies public guard labels; execution, completion, routing and budget owners call enabled/resolution at their authority boundaries.

Public surface

  • GuardDefinition, GuardResolution, guard_id, resolution and enabled provide one shared scoped policy contract.

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation
GuardDefinition 63 Immutable metadata for one named Agent Check, including its owner, default, supported scopes and meaning of bypass/resume. The registry describes available checks; each listed subsystem implements its actual detection and enforcement.
GuardDefinition.public 76 Combine structural registry metadata with the source-owned label, warning and model instruction for UI/API presentation. A missing message entry raises rather than inventing a label; returning this metadata changes no policy.
guard_id 392 Validate an exact registered check identifier for typed policy inputs and raise the catalog diagnostic for unknown names. It does not translate aliases or register new checks.
GuardResolution 409 Immutable effective enabled flag with the scope that supplied it and the retained run revision, used for enforcement and explanatory UI state.
resolution 419 Resolve one check from a state/context: unknown IDs are unavailable, disabled research proof suppresses its dependent completion checks during research, then strict boolean run overrides precede the accepted policy and registry default. Return source/revision with the value; no settings are read or mutated.
enabled 444 Return only the effective enforcement flag from resolution. Disabled-check monitoring is separate and must not be mistaken for enabled enforcement.
resolve 452 Build a full accepted snapshot by overlaying individual guard values in Global, Conversation, Prompt then Run order on registry defaults. Ignore stale/invalid stored entries, but reject unknown or non-boolean explicit prompt/run edits. Return both effective values and their sources without persisting them.
bind 477 Bind monitoring and guard policy into mutable execution context. A retained run wins over current settings, including its source map, overrides and revision; a new context resolves saved defaults only when no explicit policy is present. Return a copy of the accepted policy map.
public_state 506 Project effective guard values, scope sources, current overrides/revision, strikes and actionable recovery notices for UI consumers. The relaxed count reflects resolved flags; this projection does not apply an override or resume execution.
current_execution_policy 530 Read the context-local execution policy installed for the current call chain, defaulting to an empty context outside a bound operation.
execution_policy 538 Bind policy and its redaction settings for a nested execution scope, then restore both contexts even when the operation raises. ContextVar ownership prevents one asynchronous call's policy from becoming another's default.
RuntimePolicyError 552 Carry a named guard failure and whether execution occurred through existing ValueError handling. The identifier also serves as error_kind so callers can report the responsible check without deriving it from message prose.
